info.name: StaySync — Hotel Offer Orchestrator
info.description:
Requests and automated tests for StaySync.

Variables: `host` (default localhost), `port` (default 4000) → `baseUrl` = http://{{host}}:{{port}}.

Run order matters inside a folder (Collection Runner / newman runs top to bottom).
- Folders 1–4 run against the normal stack: `docker compose up --build`.
- Folder 5 needs the development override: `docker compose -f docker-compose.yml -f docker-compose.dev.yml up --build`.
- Folder 6 contains manual outage drills — follow the instructions in each sub-folder.

Response contract of GET /api/hotels: a JSON array of { name, price, supplier, commissionPct }.
Metadata is in headers: X-City, X-Data-Source (cache | workflow), X-Cached, X-Degraded, X-Failed-Suppliers, X-Result-Count.

item.name: 1. Health
item.description: Liveness, readiness and the full dependency report. Health checks never start workflows.

request.description: Full report: api, redis, temporal, worker (live pollers on the task queue), supplierA, supplierB. Overall status healthy | degraded (200) or unhealthy (503). Results are reused for 2s.

exec: pm.test('all dependencies healthy on a running stack', () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().status).to.eql('healthy'));

request.description: Process is alive. Checks no dependencies (stays 200 during Redis/Temporal outages).
Ready when the instance can serve /api/hotels: Redis up (cache hits) OR Temporal + a live worker (cache misses). 503 otherwise.

item.name: Temporal outage
item.description:
Run "1. Health" / "3. Hotel search" first so Delhi is cached.
Before: docker compose stop temporal
After:  docker compose start temporal   (the worker reconnects by itself)

Expected: cached cities are still served from Redis; an uncached city fails fast with 503;
/health shows temporal unhealthy and the worker as unknown (cannot be verified).
Variant: docker compose stop worker → uncached city answers 504 after the 30s workflow timeout;
/health reports the worker unhealthy once its last poll is older than 90s.
